findings.failure_mode: Missing or unreadable ledger file aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? or explicit map_err

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses Vec without bounds check after split+collect
findings.failure_mode: Empty or malformed line causes panic instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and handle None for missing delimiter; use get(0) or match on first()

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses Vec without bounds check after split+collect
findings.failure_mode: Line with only one comma-separated field panics on index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and handle the second field via match/unwrap_or; never index the split result

findings.failure_mode: Malformed numeric field in ledger crashes the parser instead of yielding a typed domain error
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ParseError::InvalidValue(e))? and propagate via Result

findings.problem: as u16 performs unchecked narrowing cast from u32
findings.failure_mode: Values above 65535 silently truncate to u16 range, corrupting ledger data without error
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ValueError::OutOfBounds)? or parse directly as u16

findings.problem: split(',').map(..).collect() allocates full Vec then indexes, instead of split_once
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per line; each line allocates a Vec<String> for just two fields
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to extract name and value parts; trim and parse each individually

findings.problem: I/O (fs::read_to_string), logging (println!), and parsing are all mixed into a single function
findings.failure_mode: Cannot test the parsing/core logic in isolation; side effects make the function non-deterministic and untestable as pure logic
findings.fix: Split into: (1) a pure fn parse_record(&str) -> Result<Record, ParseError>, (2) a shell fn load_ledgers(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> that calls fs::read_to_string, iterates lines, calls parse_record, and handles println! at the boundary

findings.problem: println! inside load_ledders is a hidden side effect in what should be data-loading logic
findings.failure_mode: Side effect in a library function produces uncontrolled stdout output; breaks deterministic behavior and testing
findings.fix: Remove println!; if logging is needed, pass a logger callback or use a typed audit event returned from the shell layer

findings.problem: Function returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures must panic
findings.failure_mode: Every external input point (file not found, I/O error, parse error) collapses to panic — no error taxonomy, no recovery path
findings.fix: Define a domain error enum (e.g. enum LedgerError { Io(std::io::Error), Parse { line: usize, field: &'static str, cause: String } }) and return Result<Vec<Record>, LedgerError>

findings.problem: No [dev-dependencies] bench section, no criterion/nightly benchmark config, and no benchmark binary
findings.failure_mode: Performance claims (or regressions) have no measurable baseline; allocations per-line are unmeasured
findings.fix: Add criterion as dev-dependency and a examples/bench.rs or benches/ benchmark for load_ledgers throughput and allocation

findings.problem: Per-line Vec<String> allocation with no profiling or allocation audit
findings.failure_mode: Unknown heap pressure; for large ledger files the O(n) per-line allocations could dominate runtime
findings.fix: Replace with split_once + &str trimming to avoid Vec<String> allocation entirely; profile with cargo-flamegraph or criterion allocs to confirm

findings.problem: No tests directory, no test functions, no test binary target in Cargo.toml
findings.failure_mode: No behavioral verification exists; all fixes are untested
findings.fix: Add tests/ directory with behavior tests covering: valid record, missing field, non-numeric value, out-of-range u16, empty file, missing file

findings.problem: No flamegraph, perf, or allocation profiling evidence for the hot path
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify that refactoring split+collect into split_once actually reduces allocations
findings.fix: Run cargo flamegraph or cargo-bench with allocation tracking before and after refactor

findings.problem: No cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test command evidence
findings.failure_mode: Code quality and correctness gates not verified by any command
findings.fix: Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, and cargo test in CI before delivery
